A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EmbodiedOcc and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 includes Appendices A and B; these are absent from the supplied v3 PDF. The available material supports comparison, including those omissions.

before.justification: v1 reports original local and embodied occupancy experiments, look-back tests, component ablations and qualitative predictions in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original occupancy experiments and adds baseline comparisons, stopping-threshold tests, voxel and depth-model controls, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds a stopping mechanism based on the fraction of Gaussians previously updated. The Gaussian memory, depth-aware refinement, confidence weighting, splatting and training losses remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of embeddings and sparse convolution document existing components rather than establish a redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate local and embodied occupancy on Occ-ScanNet, EmbodiedOcc-ScanNet and their retained mini subsets. The added controls and stopping tests reuse this coverage; they do not introduce another dataset, population or task.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 add evaluated TPVFormer, GaussianFormer and SurroundOcc comparisons for both local and embodied prediction. MonoScene and ISO remain local comparators, and SplicingOcc remains the main global comparator. The separate SplicingOcc comparison on EmbodiedOcc-ScanNet-mini is omitted.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes look-back evaluation from repeating all K frames forward to returning through K-1 frames in reverse order. Figure 5 adds stopping thresholds evaluated against the full 30-frame ground-truth region. Section 4.1 changes local evaluation wording from the box to the current frustum, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Principal splits and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a voxel-representation control, an IndoorDepth substitution, stopping-threshold analysis and runtime decomposition. Its memory-removal row largely redisplays the existing SplicingOcc comparison. Conversely, v1 Table 5's frozen-layer-count ablation disappears; only its confidence-coefficient sweep survives in Figure 6. The look-back analysis is revised, and additional appendix examples are omitted.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Gaussian confidence values and look-back revisits are method components and evaluation procedures, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the reported local IoU/mIoU of 53.95/45.48 with 53.55/45.15, alongside revised evaluation wording. Look-back scores change under different frame sequences. Numerous baseline, voxel, IndoorDepth, stopping and runtime results are added, while mini-dataset classwise comparisons and frozen-layer results are omitted. The main global result remains 51.52/42.53.

T1.justification: v3 introduces the formal confidence-ratio definition for stopping in Equation 6. Section 4.1 also corrects the global voxel-count expression to divide scene volume by (0.08 m)^3 rather than 0.08 m. The existing refinement equations and loss are substantively retained; neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add an explicit efficiency claim and broaden comparative wording beyond outperforming local prediction methods. The central contributions remain the embodied occupancy task, Gaussian-memory framework and reorganized benchmark. Expandability remains claimed in the conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking driving-method weaknesses to coarse structural modeling and absent global memory, and argues that Gaussians better support local-global interaction than voxels. It interprets the IndoorDepth test as evidence of depth-network portability and identifies image/depth backbones as runtime bottlenecks. These extend the retained depth, memory and confidence interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 omits Appendix A's benchmark-construction information, including CompleteScanNet label sourcing, nearest-neighbor transfer, interval-based frame resampling and the construction diagram. This substantially reduces documentation of the new benchmark. Conversely, Section 3.2 explains embeddings and sparse-convolution feature integration more explicitly, and Table 7 supplies component timings. The code link and principal training hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds literature on classical semantic scene completion, embodied navigation, IndoorDepth and Gaussian methods. Section 2 newly discusses SCFusion as incremental RGB-D prediction and characterizes EmbodiedScan as offline global prediction rather than continuous occupancy prediction. These refine the existing positioning around online RGB-only scene understanding.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and method exposition undergo extensive rewriting. The local prediction module becomes the local refinement module, with clearer initialization, feature-integration and memory-update subdivisions. Results and analyses are separated into Sections 4.3 and 4.4, while the supplied v3 omits the appendix sections.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 are substantially redrawn. Benchmark tables expand, the combined depth/Gaussian ablation table splits into Tables 5 and 6, and part of the confidence table becomes Figure 6. Stopping and runtime displays are added. Existing local/global visualizations move to Figures 8/7, while v1's appendix visualizations and dataset-construction diagram disappear.

improvement.justification: Broader local/global comparisons and new voxel and depth-model controls strengthen empirical support beyond v1's limited comparator set. Clearer diagrams and runtime measurements also improve assessment of the method. However, losing Appendix A's benchmark-construction details and the frozen-layer ablation reduces reproducibility and diagnostic coverage. The evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than an unqualified substantial gain.
